summary: Transit partner stripped BGP community leading to detour, TLS handshake latency and packet reorder causing streaming timeouts for dedicated customer
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightRetail (dedicated deployment in us-west-2) started seeing increased streaming disconnects and high tail latencies on March 10. Initial spikes coincide with requests being routed out through an unexpected transit path (partner AS) that appears to be stripping our BGP egress community tags.

Impact:
- Multiple streaming sessions aborted with client-observed timeouts (websocket closes, grpc stream resets).
- P95 for token response increased from ~600ms to ~3s; P99 increased up to ~12s for affected flows.
- Symptoms reproducible for both rw-8b-v1 and open/mt-6b models when routed via affected path.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: brightretail-prod-dedicated (us-west-2)
- API endpoints: prod.redwood.ai (edge anycast), downstream egress via partner transit (AS 64521)
- Observed from 2026-03-10 08:12 UTC

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send streaming generation request to customer's pinned model via prod endpoint from a client in us-west region.
2) Observe streaming connection establishment and token frames.
3) Intermittently the stream stalls during initial TLS handshake or within first 3-8 tokens; socket shows retransmits and reordering.
4) Requests routed through partner transit show the issue; same request routed through direct peering does not.

Observed behavior:
- TCP retransmits and packet reordering visible in packet captures (tcpdump) on egress node.
- TLS handshake timeouts and multiple full-handshake attempts (session resumption failures).
- Serving runtime logs show partial sends and stalled KV-cache fetches related to slow ACKs.
- No application-layer 5xx from serving runtime; issue is network/transport.

Expected behavior:
- Egress path preserves BGP community tags used for transit selection so traffic uses low-latency peering path and TLS handshakes complete within normal SLOs.

Logs / metrics / evidence:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/egress/egress-p99 (spike at 2026-03-10 08:12 UTC)
- Packet captures (redacted): s3://redwood-support-artifacts/SUP-268190/egress-tcpdump-20260310.pcap
- Edge trace id sample: trace-7b9f3c (shows retry and route via AS64521)
- Slack thread: #support - https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C01234F56/p1678552800000

Initial triage notes:
- On-call network engineer (Marco) confirmed partner AS 64521 started stripping BGP communities for a small subset of prefixes due to an upstream filter change.
- Routing team validated that when community is removed, our egress-controller selects fallback transit which results in higher RTT and occasional reordering from a congested partner POP.
- No configuration change on customer's side; problem originates in transit partner policy.

Immediate workaround applied:
- Force-route brightretail-prod-dedicated egress via direct peering (bypass partner transit) for affected prefixes at 2026-03-10 09:04 UTC. This reduced tail latencies back to expected levels and restored streaming stability.

Next steps / action items:
1) Network team to coordinate with transit partner (AS64521) to remove the filtering that strips our BGP community tags (assigned to Marco; ENG-923).
2) Implement additional telemetry in egress-controller to alert on community attrition and automatic failover to peering earlier (owner: egress-controller team).
3) Add runbook step to temporarily pin routes for dedicated customers when transit detours are detected.
4) Validate TLS session resumption behavior under transient retransmit conditions and consider increasing keepalive for streaming connection negotiation.

Customer communication plan:
- 2026-03-10 09:20 UTC: CS updated BrightRetail with temporary workaround and ETA for partner coordination.
- Will provide post-incident note once partner confirms fix and we validate stable metrics for 72 hours.
comments: 2026-03-10 08:45 UTC - Marco Chen (Network on-call): Identified transit AS 64521 applying a new upstream filter. Observed BGP community stripped for ~3% of affected prefixes. Opening contact ticket with transit NOC.
2026-03-10 09:06 UTC - Aisha Kapoor (Support): Applied temporary route pin for BrightRetail; customer reports immediate improvement. Notifying CS and SRE to coordinate with transit partner.
2026-03-11 14:12 UTC - Transit NOC (AS64521): We see a misapplied filter—we will roll back the change in the next maintenance window and provide confirmation. ETA 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC.
2026-03-12 03:30 UTC - Marco Chen: Partner reports rollback complete; monitoring shows no community strip events since 02:45 UTC. Still keeping temporary pin for 24h as precaution.
workaround: Pinned egress for brightretail-prod-dedicated to direct peering at 2026-03-10 09:04 UTC (manual route override). Customer streams restored. Recommended temporary keepalive increase on client-side if reconnection observed.
resolution_notes: Investigation confirmed transit partner filter caused BGP community attrition and detour into congested path. Partner rolled back change on 2026-03-12; we implemented detection alert and added a runbook item to pin routes for affected dedicated customers. Follow-up: ENG-923 (egress-controller improvement) and SRE postmortem scheduled.
